hints: Fill the board one column at a time and describe which cells of the current column are already occupied by a tile crossing into it.
The occupancy pattern is a bitmask with only 2^n possibilities for height n.
For each mask, place vertical tiles in the current column or horizontal tiles extending into the next, then transfer the resulting mask.
analogy: A column mask records tile halves that arrived from the previous column; fill the remaining holes before moving on.
example: For a 2-by-2 board, the two tilings are two vertical dominoes or two horizontal dominoes.
algorithm: Use profile DP over columns. Recursively fill the first empty row in the current mask: place a vertical domino if the next row is free, or a horizontal domino and set its bit in nextMask. Sum counts modulo 1,000,000,007.
correctness: Every tiling has a unique placement choice at the first uncovered cell in each column; the transitions enumerate exactly the legal possibilities without overlap.
complexity: O(m*2^n*n) time and O(2^n) memory for an n-by-m board.
